open_questions: Gaia FLAME radius 0.4867879 Rsun gives duration_ratio 1.28 vs TIC 0.4345 Rsun giving 1.44 - still above 1.5 threshold plan would refine with spectroscopy/RV to confirm eccentricity and stellar density
SNR ~12.8 with only 3 transits (expected_share 0.1909 vs observed 0.4663, p_chance 0.006956) leaves residual false-alarm risk; additional high-SNR transit needed to rule out few-event noise
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 12.7-day flat-bottomed 0.6% dip on a nearby M dwarf that repeats consistently in two sectors and three transits with no odd-even change or secondary eclipse, and no nearby star can mimic it with a small eclipse. The 3.7-4.2 Earth-radius signal is planet-sized and steady, though the duration is slightly long and the signal is marginal (SNR ~13). The best explanation is a small planet, pending a denser stellar radius and more transits.

reasons.why: Planet-sized: 3.7 Rearth with undiluted depth 6179 ppm (rp/r* 0.07861) is well below the giant-planet/small-star ambiguous range (10-22) and below 22 Rearth stellar limit.
Flat-bottomed transit favours planet over V-shaped grazing EB: v_sigma negative indicates not V-shaped.
No significant odd/even difference (depth_odd 6222 ppm vs depth_even 5853 ppm, ratio 1.1) to indicate binary at twice period.
No secondary eclipse (snr 2.48 below 5 threshold, depth 643.2 ppm similar to best_brightening_snr 2.823) against EB, even though ratio 0.088 is similar.
Depth steady across sectors (70: 5853 ppm err 664, 92: 6222 ppm err 669, chi2 0.1526) and sector_depths_by_source verdict steady, ruling out different depth in different sectors from contamination.
Three transits consistent (chi2 2.393 dof2) with mean 6036 ppm and no outliers, share_of_top3 1.0; refit snr 12.84 shows marginal but adequate signal.

Duration 3.5h modestly longer than central 2.437h (ratio 1.44 TIC, 1.28 Gaia FLAME 0.4867879 R_sun) explained by eccentricity/log_density_ratio -0.7511 or stellar radius uncertainty (Gaia GSP-Phot 0.4948), not a density mismatch per se.

No star within 1 TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can cause dip with plausible eclipse (<25%), and closest that could is 15.4 arcsec away needing 45% eclipse, plus no Gaia NEB (non_single_star 0, ruwe 1.139) and no variable flag.

ML score is low (0.06) consistent with duration mismatch and low SNR driving scorer, but specific positive evidence (flat bottom, no secondary/odd-even, steady depth, small star b=0.4017, phase_curve ratio 0.088) outweighs generic scorer for a K/M dwarf (Teff 3547K) where similar flagged signals were planets.
